meta.teaser: The mystery behind love, deuce and the strangest scoring system in sport.

page.title: Why tennis counts 15, 30, 40
page.sub: The story of tennis's strangest scoring system
page.bigIdea: You say "15-love" every match, but the numbers are about 600 years old. They may come from a clock face in medieval France.

cards.title: Points that jump by 15
cards.front: In most sports, one point is 1. In tennis, your first point is 15.
cards.back: A game goes love, 15, 30, 40, then game. You need four points and a two-point lead to win it.
cards.tryit: Watch one game of a pro match and say each score before the umpire does.

cards.title: The clock face idea
cards.front: One theory says players in old France kept score on a clock.
cards.back: Each point moved a hand a quarter turn: 15, 30, 45. Reaching 60, the top of the hour, won the game. A poem from 1435 mentions forty-five.
cards.tryit: Draw a clock. Move a pencil hand through a game you played, one quarter at a time.

cards.title: Why 45 became 40
cards.front: If it went 15, 30, 45, why do we say 40 today?
cards.back: Games must be won by two points. So the last 20 minutes split into two 10s: 40, then 50 for advantage, then 60 for game.
cards.tryit: On your clock, show what happens at deuce. Where does the hand go if you lose advantage?

cards.title: Why zero is love
cards.front: Why would a score of zero be called love?
cards.back: One idea: the French word for egg is l'oeuf, and an egg looks like 0. Another: you keep playing for the love of the game, even at zero.
cards.tryit: Ask a friend or coach which theory they believe, then tell them the other one.

cards.title: Deuce and the tiebreak
cards.front: At 40-40 the umpire says deuce. And at 6-6 in games, a tiebreak starts.
cards.back: Deuce likely comes from French for two: you need two points in a row. A 1969 Wimbledon match took over five hours, so tiebreaks spread from 1970.
cards.tryit: Play a practice tiebreak to 7. You must win by two, so keep going if it's 6-6.

words.d: A 40-40 tie in a game. You need two points in a row.
The point after deuce. Win the next point and you win the game.
A special game at 6-6, played to 7 points, win by two.
An old French game like tennis, first played with the hand.
The official who calls the score and runs the match.

quiz.q: The server has won three points and the receiver one. What's the score?
quiz.hint: Count up: love, 15, 30, then the odd one. The server's score comes first.
quiz.why: Three points is 40 and one point is 15, so it's 40-15.

quiz.q: In the clock theory, what number stood for advantage?
quiz.hint: After 40, the last 20 minutes were split into two equal steps.
quiz.why: 40 plus 10 is 50 for advantage, and another 10 reaches 60 for game.

quiz.q: Which is a real theory for why zero is called love?
opts: It was a famous player's name
It's an old word for the net
The French word for egg sounds like it
quiz.hint: Think about what shape the number zero looks like.
quiz.why: L'oeuf means egg in French, and an egg looks like a 0.

quiz.q: Why did tennis start using tiebreaks?
opts: Some matches went on for hours
quiz.hint: Remember the 1969 Wimbledon match in card 5.
quiz.why: Very long sets were tiring, so the tiebreak was made to finish sets faster.

page.think: If you could invent a new scoring system for tennis or Brawl Stars, how would it work, and what would you call zero?
